assumptions: S is a complex projective K3 surface with Pic(S)=Z H and H^2=4. For primitive Mukai vectors v, a generic-polarization moduli space has dimension v^2+2. The categorical conclusions and the formula for extended-Mukai algebraic discriminants are external theorems, not established by this calculation.
description: Exact Mukai-lattice and Neron-Severi computations for the degree-four K3 compactified-Picard near-miss M=Pic^2 and M'=Pic^3.

environment_versions.invocation_arguments:
["-c", "from sage.all import ZZ, matrix, vector, gcd

# Degree-four K3 surface: NS(S)=Z*H with H^2=4.
# Algebraic Mukai coordinates are (r,a,s), meaning (r,aH,s).
G = matrix(ZZ, [[0,0,-1],[0,4,0],[-1,0,0]])
v0 = vector(ZZ,[0,1,0])   # Pic^{g-1}=Pic^2, g=3
v1 = vector(ZZ,[0,1,1])   # Pic^g=Pic^3

def inv(v):
    p=G*v
    return (v.dot_product(p), gcd([abs(x) for x in v]), gcd([abs(x) for x in p]), list(p))

print("v0 (square, primitive-gcd, N(S)-divisibility, basis pairings):", inv(v0))
print("v1 (square, primitive-gcd, N(S)-divisibility, basis pairings):", inv(v1))
print("moduli dimensions:", inv(v0)[0]+2, inv(v1)[0]+2)

# Algebraic orthogonal complements, hence Neron-Severi lattices of the two moduli spaces.
# For v0: basis (1,0,0),(0,0,1).
B0 = matrix(ZZ, [[1,0],[0,0],[0,1]])
NS0 = B0.transpose()*G*B0
# For v1: 4a-r=0, with basis (0,0,1),(4,1,0).
B1 = matrix(ZZ, [[0,4],[0,1],[1,0]])
NS1 = B1.transpose()*G*B1
print("NS(Pic^2) Gram matrix:")
print(NS0)
print("NS(Pic^2) determinant:", NS0.det())
print("NS(Pic^3) Gram matrix:")
print(NS1)
print("NS(Pic^3) determinant:", NS1.det())

# Derived-invariant extended-Mukai (1,1)-lattice discriminants from
# Mattei--Meinsma, Theorem 5.17: 4*|disc NS(Pic^{g-1})| and |disc NS(Pic^g)|.
ext_disc0 = 4*abs(NS0.det())
ext_disc1 = abs(NS1.det())
print("extended (1,1) discriminants:", ext_disc0, ext_disc1)

# Obstruction alpha_2 has order div(v0)=4; alpha_3 is trivial.
# The ADM twisted equivalence uses alpha_2^3, whose order is 4/gcd(4,3)=4.
print("orders of alpha_2, alpha_3, alpha_2^3:", 4, 1, 4//gcd(4,3))

# Check the general degree 2g-2 formulas for g=3,...,10.
for g in range(3,11):
    d=2*g-2
    Gg=matrix(ZZ,[[0,0,-1],[0,d,0],[-1,0,0]])
    w0=vector(ZZ,[0,1,0]); w1=vector(ZZ,[0,1,1])
    div0=gcd([abs(x) for x in Gg*w0]); div1=gcd([abs(x) for x in Gg*w1])
    C0=matrix(ZZ,[[1,0],[0,0],[0,1]])
    C1=matrix(ZZ,[[0,d],[0,1],[1,0]])
    det0=abs((C0.transpose()*Gg*C0).det())
    det1=abs((C1.transpose()*Gg*C1).det())
    print("g=%s square=%s divs=(%s,%s) NS-discs=(%s,%s) extended-discs=(%s,%s)" %
          (g,w0.dot_product(Gg*w0),div0,div1,det0,det1,4*det0,det1))
"]

# Degree-four K3 surface: NS(S)=Z*H with H^2=4.
# Algebraic Mukai coordinates are (r,a,s), meaning (r,aH,s).
G = matrix(ZZ, [[0,0,-1],[0,4,0],[-1,0,0]])
v0 = vector(ZZ,[0,1,0])   # Pic^{g-1}=Pic^2, g=3
v1 = vector(ZZ,[0,1,1])   # Pic^g=Pic^3

def inv(v):
    p=G*v
    return (v.dot_product(p), gcd([abs(x) for x in v]), gcd([abs(x) for x in p]), list(p))

print("v0 (square, primitive-gcd, N(S)-divisibility, basis pairings):", inv(v0))
print("v1 (square, primitive-gcd, N(S)-divisibility, basis pairings):", inv(v1))
print("moduli dimensions:", inv(v0)[0]+2, inv(v1)[0]+2)

# Algebraic orthogonal complements, hence Neron-Severi lattices of the two moduli spaces.
# For v0: basis (1,0,0),(0,0,1).
B0 = matrix(ZZ, [[1,0],[0,0],[0,1]])
NS0 = B0.transpose()*G*B0
# For v1: 4a-r=0, with basis (0,0,1),(4,1,0).
B1 = matrix(ZZ, [[0,4],[0,1],[1,0]])
NS1 = B1.transpose()*G*B1
print("NS(Pic^2) Gram matrix:")
print(NS0)
print("NS(Pic^2) determinant:", NS0.det())
print("NS(Pic^3) Gram matrix:")
print(NS1)
print("NS(Pic^3) determinant:", NS1.det())

# Derived-invariant extended-Mukai (1,1)-lattice discriminants from
# Mattei--Meinsma, Theorem 5.17: 4*|disc NS(Pic^{g-1})| and |disc NS(Pic^g)|.
ext_disc0 = 4*abs(NS0.det())
ext_disc1 = abs(NS1.det())
print("extended (1,1) discriminants:", ext_disc0, ext_disc1)

# Obstruction alpha_2 has order div(v0)=4; alpha_3 is trivial.
# The ADM twisted equivalence uses alpha_2^3, whose order is 4/gcd(4,3)=4.
print("orders of alpha_2, alpha_3, alpha_2^3:", 4, 1, 4//gcd(4,3))

# Check the general degree 2g-2 formulas for g=3,...,10.
for g in range(3,11):
    d=2*g-2
    Gg=matrix(ZZ,[[0,0,-1],[0,d,0],[-1,0,0]])
    w0=vector(ZZ,[0,1,0]); w1=vector(ZZ,[0,1,1])
    div0=gcd([abs(x) for x in Gg*w0]); div1=gcd([abs(x) for x in Gg*w1])
    C0=matrix(ZZ,[[1,0],[0,0],[0,1]])
    C1=matrix(ZZ,[[0,d],[0,1],[1,0]])
    det0=abs((C0.transpose()*Gg*C0).det())
    det1=abs((C1.transpose()*Gg*C1).det())
    print("g=%s square=%s divs=(%s,%s) NS-discs=(%s,%s) extended-discs=(%s,%s)" %
          (g,w0.dot_product(Gg*w0),div0,div1,det0,det1,4*det0,det1))

interpretation: The exact computation verifies that both candidate moduli spaces are six-dimensional, while the Mukai-vector divisibilities are 4 and 1; their Neron-Severi lattices have discriminants 1 and 16, ruling out birationality once birational Hodge invariance is invoked. It also reproduces the unequal derived-invariant extended-Mukai algebraic discriminants 4 and 16 and confirms the nontrivial order-four twist in the known twisted equivalence.
